result:
**Verdict: PASS. No new findings, and I raise none that blocks DG5.**

I reviewed candidate `sha256:33188e9e…` (2194 files, source `12dc33e`, freeze commit `1932faa`). I confirmed the candidate ID on a complete clone at the start and again at the end; HEAD never moved. The record is at `docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-7/code-security-reviewer.json` and validates against the review schema. With no findings there is no sidecar.

**What changed since round 6.** Only web code changed. The API, worker, migrations, OpenAPI contract and requirement register are byte-identical to round 6, so my earlier review of them still applies. I re-confirmed it by running the full suites and all my probes again.

**The D-181 hook (`queries.ts:230-283`).** It is sound on all four points I was asked to judge:
- **Termination:** it stops on three separate conditions:
  - the server returns no next cursor;
  - the server repeats a cursor, which is an error;
  - 1000 pages are reached, which is also an error, never a shortened list.

  The server's paging is strictly ordered and its cursors only work with the filters they were issued for.
- **Cancellation:** the abort signal reaches every page request. My new web probe shows that aborting or leaving the screen mid-list really stops further requests.
- **Error handling:** one failed page fails the whole list, so a picker never shows a partial list. Pages from two different signed-in users are never combined after a session change.
- **Authorization scope:** the hook adds no new endpoint; every page is filtered on the server. My new integration probe follows the cursor across 3 pages:
  - a business-unit-scoped user gets exactly that unit's transformations (250);
  - an organization-wide user gets that organization's 290;
  - a cursor replayed by another organization returns only that organization's rows;
  - a cursor reused with different filters is refused (400);
  - a technical admin with no business role gets an empty list.

  Three deliberately broken versions of the hook were each caught by the tests.

**The D-182 e2e failure.** The failing health-check step runs on a page that does not use the new hook. I found no code path linking the two, so D-182's "cause not established" disclosure is accurate. qa is assigned to examine it; I did not run the web e2e suite.

**Checks run:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Build, typecheck, lint, OpenAPI lint (846 operations), no-CDN, format | all exit 0 |
| Unit tests, Node 24 | 2341 + 1722 + 259 passed, 2 skipped by design |
| Unit tests, Node 22 | passed on a re-run (see disclosure below) |
| Integration, locale unset | 319 files, 3076 passed, 1 skipped by design |
| Integration, C.UTF-8 | same totals, run as two halves |
| Probes (7 from round 6 + 1 new) | 48/48 |
| Prior-gate validators (DG4–DG1) and DG5 register | pass |
| Pending-test lists | all empty |

The integration runs include the contract test and migrations 0001→0097. The permission sweep figures are identical to round 6: the read-only auditor gets 0 successful writes out of 90, and the technical admin gets 0 successful reads out of 40.

**Disclosed in the record:**
- **Node 22 first run:** all 2341 `unit-node` tests passed, but the run exited 1 because of one Vitest internal timeout under machine load around 20 on 4 CPUs. I re-ran that project alone: clean, exit 0. Both logs are kept.
- **C.UTF-8 split:** I ran it as `--shard=1/2` and `2/2` because a single run would have exceeded my 2-hour command limit. The first launch of the first half never started (wrong working directory, exit 127) and was relaunched at once.
- **`pnpm deps:verify`:** this extra command, not a required check, needs the live package registry and never returned without network. It was stopped at its time limit and is recorded as the declared registry residual.
- **My new picker probe:** it needed two fixes to my own fixture and expectations before its final passing run. Neither was a product defect.
- **Assignment template errors:** the assignment says task R5 and round 5. The record uses round 7, as the path and run ID require.
- **Remaining environmental items:** live registry (D-057), live CI (D-058), and Keycloak / a real demo IdP (D-049).

**Observations, not findings:**
- When a list is sorted by last update, a transformation edited while the list is loading can be missing until the next refresh. This is inherent to cursor paging and can never produce duplicates.
- Vite's existing warning that the main bundle is over 500 kB (1,582 kB, the same as in round 6).

Evidence, scripts and probes are under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/code-security/round-7/`; the clone and store copy were deleted.
